metadata.title: jeddyhub/balinski (Lean blueprint)

extraction_notes.note: Definition 'names' is a glossary of Lean declarations with several fragments that are not sentences (e.g. 'The dimension of a pointed cone.'); kept as one definition node.
Stated in a proposition environment but its content defines a simplicial cone; retyped to definition.

All results are standard convex-geometry facts restated without citation, so they are origin external (standard, uncited) while their proofs are paper; consequently no rigor field is set, though several proofs are one-line sketches ('should be a simple Span-induction').
Section 1.4 opening sentence ('We define faces ... main goal ...') is motivation and gets no node; it informed the main flags on LP7 and PrP22.

metadata.extraction_comment: Many propositions in 1.2-1.5 are blueprint stubs without proofs; several statements contain Lean-isms (f.map, oplus_p) copied verbatim.

nodes.name: Dual vector spaces N and M over an ordered field
nodes.statement: We work with a two mutually dual finite-dimensional vector spaces \( N \) and \( M \) over a linearly ordered field \( \Bbbk \).

nodes.name: Perfect pairing
nodes.statement: This means, we have a bilinear pairing \( \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle \colon N \times M \to \Bbbk \) such that the induced maps \( M \to \Hom(N,\Bbbk) \) and \( N \to \Hom(N,\Bbbk) \) are both bijective (this is also known as a \emph{perfect pairing}).
differentia: the induced maps \( M \to \Hom(N,\Bbbk) \) and \( N \to \Hom(N,\Bbbk) \) are both bijective
nodes.statement_short: A bilinear pairing $N\times M\to\Bbbk$ whose induced maps to the duals are bijective.

nodes.name: Non-negative scalars
nodes.statement: Since \( \Bbbk \) is linearly ordered, we can define the non-negative scalars \(\Bbbk_{\geq 0} = \{t \in \Bbbk \mid t \geq 0 \} \subseteq \Bbbk\).

nodes.name: Non-negative scalars form a semifield
nodes.statement: This is a \emph{semifield}, i.e. a commutative semiring, in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

nodes.name: Hyperplane, halfspace, dimension, full-dimensional, k-faces
nodes.statement: A {\bf hyperplane} is the perp space of a point. A {\bf halfspace} is the dual of a point. The dimension of the module the cone is a submodule of. The {\bf dimension} of a pointed cone. A polyhedral cone is {\bf full-dimensional} if its dimension is the same as the dimension of the ambient space. The set of all \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyheadral cone. For each \(k\) gives the number of \(k\)-dimensional faces of a polyheadral cone.
nodes.statement_short: Glossary: hyperplane = perp of a point, halfspace = dual of a point, dimension, full-dimensional cones, k-dimensional faces and their counts.
nodes.label: names

nodes.name: Pointed cone
nodes.statement: A {\bf pointed cone} \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a \( \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \)-submodule of \( N \).
nodes.label: pointed-cone

nodes.name: Pointy cone
nodes.statement: A {\bf pointy cone} \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a \( \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \)-submodule of \( N \) that does not contain a nontrivial linear space.
differentia: does not contain a nontrivial linear space
nodes.label: pointy-cone

nodes.name: Cone generated by a set
nodes.statement: For a set \( S \subseteq N \), the {\bf cone generated by \( S \)} is the pointed cone \[ \Cone(S) := \Span_{\Bbbk_{\geq 0}}(S) \subseteq N. \]
nodes.label: cone-span

nodes.name: Finitely generated cone
nodes.statement: A pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is called {\bf finitely generated}, if \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) for some finite set \( S \subseteq N \).
differentia: \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) for some finite set \( S \subseteq N \)
nodes.label: cone-finitely-generated

nodes.name: Dual cone
nodes.statement: For a set \( S \subseteq M \), the {\bf dual cone of \( S \)} is the pointed cone \[ S^\vee := \{x \in N \mid \forall y \in S, \langle x, y \rangle \geq 0 \} \subseteq N. \]
nodes.label: dual-cone

nodes.name: Polyhedral cone
nodes.statement: Another word for finitely generated cone with a finitely generated canonical dual.
differentia: with a finitely generated canonical dual
nodes.label: polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Zero cone is polyhedral
nodes.statement: The zero-space \( \{0\} \subseteq N \) is a polyhedral cone.
conclusions: The zero-space \( \{0\} \subseteq N \) is a polyhedral cone
nodes.label: bot-polyhedral

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: If \( S \subseteq M \) is a finite \( \Bbbk \)-basis of \( M \), then \( \{0\} = (S \cup -S)^\vee \).
nodes.statement_short: Write $\{0\}$ as the dual of a basis together with its negatives.

nodes.name: Full space is polyhedral
nodes.statement: The full space is a polyhedral cone.
conclusions: The full space is a polyhedral cone
nodes.label: all-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Halfspaces are polyhedral
nodes.statement: Any halfspace is a polyhedral cone.
conclusions: Any halfspace is a polyhedral cone
nodes.label: halfspace-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Linear subspaces are polyhedral
nodes.statement: Any linear subspace is a polyhedral cone.
conclusions: Any linear subspace is a polyhedral cone
nodes.label: linear-subspace-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Dual of a finitely generated cone is polyhedral
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subset N \) is finitely generated, then \( \sigma^\vee \subset M \) is polyhedral.
nodes.label: dual-polyhedral

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5
nodes.statement: Let \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) for \( S \subseteq N \). We need to show \( \Cone(S)^\vee = S^\vee \). The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious, as \( S \subseteq \Cone(S) \). The opposite inclusion can be shown by induction on the general element of \( \Cone(S) \).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\Cone(S)^\vee = S^\vee$; one inclusion is obvious, the other by induction on elements of $\Cone(S)$.

nodes.name: Double dual
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral, then \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = \sigma \).
nodes.label: double-dual-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Proof of Double dual
nodes.statement: For any set \( S \subseteq N \) it is trivial to show \( S^{\vee\vee\vee} = S^{\vee} \). The claim follows since \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for a finite set \( S \subseteq N \).
nodes.statement_short: Use the triple-dual identity $S^{\vee\vee\vee}=S^\vee$ with $\sigma=S^\vee$.

nodes.name: Fourier-Motzkin elimination
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a polyhedral cone and \( w \in N \), then \( \sigma + \Cone(\{w\}) \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.statement_short: Adding one generator to a polyhedral cone keeps it polyhedral.
nodes.label: fourier-motzkin

nodes.name: Proof of Fourier-Motzkin elimination
nodes.statement: Write \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for a finite \( S \subseteq M \). Define \[ T\ :=\ \{x \in S \mid 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle \}\ \cup\ \{y \langle x, w \rangle - x \langle y, w \rangle \mid x, y \in S, 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle, \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \}\ \subseteq\ M. \] Note that \( T \) is finite. We claim \( S^{\vee} + \Cone(\{w\}) = T^{\vee} \). Clearly \( T \subseteq \Cone(S) \), hence \( S^{\vee} = \Cone(S)^{\vee} \subseteq T^{\vee} \). Also clear is \( w \in T^{\vee} \), hence \( S^{\vee} + \Cone(\{w\}) \subset T^{\vee} \). For the reverse inclusion, let \( v \in T^\vee \). We need to show \( v - uw \in S^\vee \) for some \( u \in \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \). If there is no \( y \in S \) with both \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \) and \( \langle y, v \rangle < 0 \), we can easily see that \( u = 0 \) works, i.e. \( T^{\vee} \subseteq S^{\vee} \). Otherwise, we set \[ u\ :=\ \max_{\substack{y \in S \\ \langle y, w \rangle < 0}} \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle}, \] which is then well-defined and non-negative. We need to show \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) for all \( z \in S \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle < 0 \), this follows from maximality of \( u \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle = 0 \), the claim follows from \( z \in T \) and \( v \in T^{\vee} \). Lastly, assume \( \langle z, w \rangle > 0 \) and fix \( y \in S \) such that \( u = \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle} \). In particular, \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \). Then the claim \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) is equivalent to \[ \langle y, v \rangle \langle z, w \rangle \geq \langle z, v \rangle \langle y, w \rangle. \] But \( y \langle z, w \rangle - z \langle y, w \rangle \in T \), hence the claim follows from \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Construct the finite set $T$ of Fourier-Motzkin combinations and show $S^\vee+\Cone(\{w\})=T^\vee$. The reverse inclusion picks $u$ as a maximal ratio and checks three sign cases of $\langle z,w\rangle$.

nodes.name: Finitely generated cones are polyhedral
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \in N \) is finitely generated, then it is polyhedral.
nodes.label: polyhedral-of-fg

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 8
nodes.statement: Write \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) and use induction on the size of \( S \): For \( S = \emptyset \), we use~\ref{bot-polyhedral} and the induction step is~\ref{fourier-motzkin}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of generators: zero cone base case, Fourier-Motzkin step.

nodes.name: Double dual of a finite set
nodes.statement: For a finite set \( S \subseteq N \), we have \( S^{\vee\vee} = \Cone(S) \).
nodes.label: double-dual-finite-set

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 9
nodes.statement: The cone \( \sigma := \Cone(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. Furthermore, we have \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = S^{\vee\vee} \). Now apply~\ref{double-dual-polyhedral-cone}.
nodes.statement_short: $\Cone(S)$ is polyhedral, so the double dual theorem applies.

nodes.name: Polyhedral = Finitely generated
nodes.statement: A pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is finitely generated iff it is polyhedral.
conclusions: \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is finitely generated iff it is polyhedral
nodes.label: polyhedral-iff-fg

nodes.name: Proof of Polyhedral = Finitely generated
nodes.statement: The implication ``\( \Rightarrow \)'' is Proposition~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. For the converse, assume \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for some finite \( S \subseteq M \). Then \( \Cone(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. Thus we find a finite \( T \subseteq N \) with \( \Cone(S) = T^\vee \). We obtain \[ \sigma = S^{\vee} = \Cone(S)^\vee = T^{\vee\vee} = \Cone(T), \] where the last equality is due to~\ref{double-dual-finite-set}. Thus \( \sigma \) is finitely generated.
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction is Proposition 8; conversely write $\sigma=S^\vee=\Cone(S)^\vee=T^{\vee\vee}=\Cone(T)$.

nodes.name: Dual of a polyhedral cone is polyhedral
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral, then \( \sigma^\vee \subseteq M \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: dual-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 11
nodes.statement: \ref{dual-polyhedral} \( + \) \ref{polyhedral-iff-fg}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 5 with Polyhedral = Finitely generated.

nodes.name: Polyhedral cone is pointy cone plus linear subspace
nodes.statement: Every polyhedral cone can be written as the minkowski sum of a pointy cone and a linear subspace.
conclusions: can be written as the minkowski sum of a pointy cone and a linear subspace
nodes.label: pointy-linear-sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Linear image of a polyhedral cone
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral and \(f : N -> M\) is a linear map, then \( f.map \sigma \subseteq M \) is polyhedral too.
assumptions: \(f : N -> M\) is a linear map
nodes.label: linear-transformation-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Sum of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then \( \sigma + \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Direct sum of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, the direct sum \( \sigma \oplus_p \tau \) is polyhedral too.
conclusions: the direct sum \( \sigma \oplus_p \tau \) is polyhedral too
nodes.label: direct-sum-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Join of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, their join is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: join-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Intersection of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then \( \sigma \cap \tau \) is polyhedral too.
nodes.label: intersection-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Product of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then the cartesian product \( \sigma \prod \tau \) is polyhedral too.
conclusions: the cartesian product \( \sigma \prod \tau \) is polyhedral too
nodes.label: product-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Convex hull
nodes.statement: For a set $S \subseteq N$, the {\bf convex hull of $S$} is $$\Conv(S) := \left\{\sum_{u \in S} \lambda_u | \lambda_u \ge 0, \sum_u \lambda_u = 1\right\}$$
nodes.label: convex-hull

nodes.name: Convex hull of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma, \tau \subseteq N \) are polyhedral, then the convex hull of the two is polyhedral too.
conclusions: the convex hull of the two is polyhedral too
nodes.label: convex-hull-polyhedral-cone

nodes.name: Lattice of polyhedral cones
nodes.statement: Polyhedral cones for a lattice under intersections and convex hulls (its the same lattice as on pointed cones).
conclusions: Polyhedral cones for a lattice under intersections and convex hulls (its the same lattice as on pointed cones).
nodes.label: polyhedra-lattice

nodes.name: Simplicial cone
nodes.statement: A simplicial cone \(\sigma\) is a polyhedral cone that can be generated by \(dim (\sigma)\) many generators.
differentia: can be generated by \(dim (\sigma)\) many generators
nodes.label: simplicial-cone

nodes.name: Perp space
nodes.statement: For any subset \( A \subseteq M \), we define the \emph{perp space} \[ A^{\perp}\ :=\ \{v \in N\ \mid\ \forall u \in A, \langle v, u \rangle = 0\}, \] which is a pointed cone in \( N \). We also write \( u^{\perp} := \{u\}^{\perp} \).
nodes.label: perp

nodes.name: Perp equals dual for sets closed under negation
nodes.statement: If \( A \subseteq M \) is closed under negation (for instance, \( A \subseteq M \) a \( \Bbbk \)-submodule), then \( A^{\perp} = A^{\vee} \).
assumptions: \( A \subseteq M \) is closed under negation
nodes.label: perp-closed-negation

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: \( A^{\perp} \subseteq A^{\vee} \) is clear. Let \( x \in A^{\vee} \) and \( a \in A \). then \( \langle x, a \rangle \geq 0 \) and \( -\langle x, a \rangle = \langle x, -a \rangle \geq 0 \). Hence \( \langle x, a \rangle = 0 \) and \( x \in A^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: An element of $A^\vee$ pairs non-negatively with $a$ and $-a$, hence to zero.

nodes.name: Face of a cone
nodes.statement: A \emph{face} of a pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is the intersection of \( \sigma \) with some hyperplane \( u^{\perp} \) for \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \). We write \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) if \( \tau \) is a face of \( \sigma \) and \( \tau \prec \sigma \) if \( \tau \) is a \emph{proper} face, i.e. \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) and \( \tau \neq \sigma \).
nodes.genus: intersection of \( \sigma \) with some hyperplane \( u^{\perp} \)
nodes.statement_short: A face is $\sigma\cap u^\perp$ for $u\in\sigma^\vee$; notation $\preceq$ and $\prec$ for faces and proper faces.
nodes.label: face

nodes.name: Cone intersected with a supporting hyperplane
nodes.statement: For any subset \( S \subseteq N \) and \( u \in S^{\vee} \), we have \[ \Cone(S) \cap u^{\perp} = \Cone(S \cap u^{\perp}). \]
nodes.label: cone-inter-perp

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 21
nodes.statement: Both inclusions should be a simple Span-induction.
nodes.statement_short: Span-induction for both inclusions.

nodes.name: Faces of polyhedral cones are polyhedral
nodes.statement: A face of a polyhedral cone is polyhedral.
assumptions: A face of a polyhedral cone
nodes.label: face-polyhedral

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Use \ref{cone-inter-perp} and the fact that if \( S \) is finite, so is \( S \cap u^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 21; $S\cap u^\perp$ is finite when $S$ is.

nodes.name: Polyhedral cones have finitely many faces
nodes.statement: A polyhedral cone has only finitely many faces.
nodes.label: faces-polyhedral-cone-finite

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: By \ref{face-polyhedral}, a face of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) is of the form \( \Cone(S') \) for some \( S' \subseteq S \). Being finite, \( S \) has only finitely many subsets, which shows the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Faces are cones on subsets of the finite generating set.

nodes.name: Intersection of faces
nodes.statement: If \( \sigma \) is a pointed cone, then the intersection of two faces of \( \sigma \) is a again face of \( \sigma \).
conclusions: the intersection of two faces of \( \sigma \) is a again face of \( \sigma \)
nodes.label: face-intersection

nodes.name: Proof of Intersection of faces
nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) and \( \tau' = \sigma \cap \tau'^{\perp} \) be faces. We claim that \( \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \cap u'^{\perp} = \sigma \cap (u + u')^{\perp} \). The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious. For the converse, suppose \( v \in \sigma \) with \( \langle v, u \rangle + \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \). Since \( u, u' \in \sigma^{\vee} \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle v, u \rangle = \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \).
nodes.statement_short: Show $\sigma\cap u^\perp\cap u'^\perp=\sigma\cap(u+u')^\perp$ using non-negativity of both summands.

nodes.name: Dual of a face
nodes.statement: Let \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) be a face of a pointed cone. Then \( \tau^{\vee} = \tau^{\perp} + \sigma^{\vee} \).
assumptions: \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) be a face of a pointed cone
nodes.label: face-dual-eq-sum

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: It's easy to show that \( \tau = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau) \cap \sigma^{\vee} \). Dualising gives \( \tau^{\vee} = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} + \sigma^{\vee} \). Apply~\ref{perp-closed-negation} to get \( \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\perp} = \tau^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: Write $\tau$ as span intersect $\sigma^\vee$, dualise, and identify the dual of the span with $\tau^\perp$ by Lemma 1.

nodes.name: Face of a face
nodes.statement: A face of a face of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma \) is again a face of \( \sigma \).
conclusions: A face of a face of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma \) is again a face of \( \sigma \)
nodes.label: face-face

nodes.name: Proof of Face of a face
nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) with \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \) with \( v \in \tau^{\vee} \). By \ref{face-dual-eq-sum}, we can write \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) with \( v_1 \in \tau^{\perp} \) and \( v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \). Then \( u + v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and we claim \( \rho = \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \). For ``\( \subseteq \)'', let \( x \in \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \). Since \( x \in \tau \), we get \( \langle x, u \rangle = 0 \) and \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). Since \( x \in v^{\perp} \), also \( \langle x, v \rangle = 0 \), which by \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) implies \( \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, u + v_2 \rangle = 0 \). For the converse, assume \( x \in \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \), i.e. \( \langle x, u \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). Since both \( u, v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( x \in \sigma \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle x, u \rangle = \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). This implies \( x \in \tau \), thus also \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, v \rangle = \langle x, v_1 \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \), thus \( x \in \rho \).
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $v=v_1+v_2$ by Lemma 5 and show $\rho=\sigma\cap(u+v_2)^\perp$ by double inclusion.

nodes.name: Faces form a partial order
nodes.statement: In particular, Lemma~\ref{face-face} establishes a partial order on the set of faces of a polyhedral cone \( \sigma \) (written \( \faces(\sigma) \)).
nodes.statement_short: The face relation is a partial order on the faces of a polyhedral cone, denoted $\faces(\sigma)$.
conclusions: Lemma~\ref{face-face} establishes a partial order on the set of faces

nodes.name: Face poset is finite
nodes.statement: It is finite by ~\ref{faces-polyhedral-cone-finite}.

nodes.name: Face lattice
nodes.statement: Given a polyhedral cone, the partial order on its faces is a lattice. We call it the \emph{face lattice} of the cone.
conclusions: the partial order on its faces is a lattice
nodes.label: face-lattice

nodes.name: Proof of Face order is a lattice
nodes.statement: Top is the entire cone, bot is the empty cone.
nodes.statement_short: Identify top and bottom elements.

nodes.name: Face lattice is graded
nodes.statement: Given a polyhedral cone, the partial order on its faces is graded.
conclusions: the partial order on its faces is graded
nodes.label: face-lattice-graded

nodes.name: Proof of Face lattice is graded
nodes.statement: The grading is given by the number of faces of this face.
nodes.statement_short: Grade by the number of faces of a face.

nodes.name: Combinatorial Equivalence
nodes.statement: Two polyhedral cones are \emph{combinatorially equivalent} if there is an order isomorphism between their face lattices.
differentia: there is an order isomorphism between their face lattices
nodes.label: combinatorial-equivalence

nodes.name: Duality of face lattices
nodes.statement: Face lattices of dual cones are dual to each other.
conclusions: Face lattices of dual cones are dual to each other.
nodes.label: dual-face-lattice

nodes.name: Face lattice of a face
nodes.statement: The face lattice of a face is isomorphic to a lower interval of the face lattice of a polyhedral cone.
conclusions: The face lattice of a face is isomorphic to a lower interval of the face lattice of a polyhedral cone.
nodes.label: face-face-lattice

nodes.name: Linear transformations preserve combinatorial equivalence
nodes.statement: Linear transformaions preserve combinatorial equivalence. There is an iso that should be provided
nodes.label: ombinatorial-equivalence-linear-transformaions

nodes.name: Polar cone
nodes.statement: For a pointed cone \( \sigma \), the {\bf polar cone of \( \sigma \)} is the pointed cone \[ S^\circ := \{x \in \sigma \mid \forall y \in \sigma, \langle x, y \rangle \leq 0 \} \]
nodes.label: polar-cone

nodes.name: Polytope
nodes.statement: A {\bf polytope} is a set that can be written as $\Conv(S)$ for some finite set $S$.
differentia: can be written as $\Conv(S)$ for some finite set $S$
nodes.label: polytope

nodes.name: Reduce to dual identity
nodes.statement: Let \( \sigma = \Cone(S) \) for \( S \subseteq N \). We need to show \( \Cone(S)^\vee = S^\vee \). The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious, as \( S \subseteq \Cone(S) \).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\Cone(S)^\vee=S^\vee$; the forward inclusion is obvious.

nodes.name: Reverse inclusion by induction
nodes.statement: The opposite inclusion can be shown by induction on the general element of \( \Cone(S) \).
nodes.statement_short: Reverse inclusion by induction on elements of $\Cone(S)$.

nodes.name: Define the set T
nodes.statement: Write \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for a finite \( S \subseteq M \). Define \[ T\ :=\ \{x \in S \mid 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle \}\ \cup\ \{y \langle x, w \rangle - x \langle y, w \rangle \mid x, y \in S, 0 \leq \langle x, w \rangle, \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \}\ \subseteq\ M. \] Note that \( T \) is finite.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\sigma=S^\vee$ and define the finite set $T$.

nodes.name: Claim: dual of T
nodes.statement: We claim \( S^{\vee} + \Cone(\{w\}) = T^{\vee} \). Clearly \( T \subseteq \Cone(S) \), hence \( S^{\vee} = \Cone(S)^{\vee} \subseteq T^{\vee} \). Also clear is \( w \in T^{\vee} \), hence \( S^{\vee} + \Cone(\{w\}) \subset T^{\vee} \). For the reverse inclusion, let \( v \in T^\vee \). We need to show \( v - uw \in S^\vee \) for some \( u \in \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \). If there is no \( y \in S \) with both \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \) and \( \langle y, v \rangle < 0 \), we can easily see that \( u = 0 \) works, i.e. \( T^{\vee} \subseteq S^{\vee} \). Otherwise, we set \[ u\ :=\ \max_{\substack{y \in S \\ \langle y, w \rangle < 0}} \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle}, \] which is then well-defined and non-negative. We need to show \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) for all \( z \in S \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle < 0 \), this follows from maximality of \( u \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle = 0 \), the claim follows from \( z \in T \) and \( v \in T^{\vee} \). Lastly, assume \( \langle z, w \rangle > 0 \) and fix \( y \in S \) such that \( u = \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle} \). In particular, \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \). Then the claim \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) is equivalent to \[ \langle y, v \rangle \langle z, w \rangle \geq \langle z, v \rangle \langle y, w \rangle. \] But \( y \langle z, w \rangle - z \langle y, w \rangle \in T \), hence the claim follows from \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Claim $S^\vee+\Cone(\{w\})=T^\vee$ and prove it.

nodes.name: Forward inclusion
nodes.statement: Clearly \( T \subseteq \Cone(S) \), hence \( S^{\vee} = \Cone(S)^{\vee} \subseteq T^{\vee} \). Also clear is \( w \in T^{\vee} \), hence \( S^{\vee} + \Cone(\{w\}) \subset T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Forward inclusion via $T\subseteq\Cone(S)$ and $w\in T^\vee$.

nodes.name: Set up reverse inclusion
nodes.statement: For the reverse inclusion, let \( v \in T^\vee \). We need to show \( v - uw \in S^\vee \) for some \( u \in \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \).
nodes.statement_short: For $v\in T^\vee$, reduce to finding $u\ge0$ with $v-uw\in S^\vee$.

nodes.name: Case u = 0
nodes.statement: If there is no \( y \in S \) with both \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \) and \( \langle y, v \rangle < 0 \), we can easily see that \( u = 0 \) works, i.e. \( T^{\vee} \subseteq S^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: If no $y$ has both pairings negative, $u=0$ works.

nodes.name: Otherwise: maximal ratio
nodes.statement: Otherwise, we set \[ u\ :=\ \max_{\substack{y \in S \\ \langle y, w \rangle < 0}} \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle}, \] which is then well-defined and non-negative. We need to show \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) for all \( z \in S \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle < 0 \), this follows from maximality of \( u \). If \( \langle z, w \rangle = 0 \), the claim follows from \( z \in T \) and \( v \in T^{\vee} \). Lastly, assume \( \langle z, w \rangle > 0 \) and fix \( y \in S \) such that \( u = \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle} \). In particular, \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \). Then the claim \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) is equivalent to \[ \langle y, v \rangle \langle z, w \rangle \geq \langle z, v \rangle \langle y, w \rangle. \] But \( y \langle z, w \rangle - z \langle y, w \rangle \in T \), hence the claim follows from \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise take $u$ as the maximal ratio and verify the inequality for all $z\in S$.

nodes.name: Define u
nodes.statement: Otherwise, we set \[ u\ :=\ \max_{\substack{y \in S \\ \langle y, w \rangle < 0}} \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle}, \] which is then well-defined and non-negative. We need to show \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) for all \( z \in S \).
nodes.statement_short: Define $u$ as a maximum of ratios and state what must be shown.

nodes.name: Case negative pairing
nodes.statement: If \( \langle z, w \rangle < 0 \), this follows from maximality of \( u \).
nodes.statement_short: Negative case follows from maximality of $u$.

nodes.name: Case zero pairing
nodes.statement: If \( \langle z, w \rangle = 0 \), the claim follows from \( z \in T \) and \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Zero case: $z\in T$.

nodes.name: Case positive pairing
nodes.statement: Lastly, assume \( \langle z, w \rangle > 0 \) and fix \( y \in S \) such that \( u = \frac{\langle y, v \rangle}{\langle y, w \rangle} \). In particular, \( \langle y, w \rangle < 0 \). Then the claim \( u \langle z, w \rangle \leq \langle z, v \rangle \) is equivalent to \[ \langle y, v \rangle \langle z, w \rangle \geq \langle z, v \rangle \langle y, w \rangle. \] But \( y \langle z, w \rangle - z \langle y, w \rangle \in T \), hence the claim follows from \( v \in T^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Positive case: reduce to an inequality given by a combination lying in $T$.

nodes.name: Cone(S) is polyhedral
nodes.statement: The cone \( \sigma := \Cone(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}.
nodes.statement_short: $\Cone(S)$ is polyhedral by Proposition 8.

nodes.name: Same double dual
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we have \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = S^{\vee\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Double duals of $\sigma$ and $S$ agree.

nodes.name: Apply double dual
nodes.statement: Now apply~\ref{double-dual-polyhedral-cone}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the double dual proposition.

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement: The implication ``\( \Rightarrow \)'' is Proposition~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}.
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction is Proposition 8.

nodes.name: Converse: Cone(S) polyhedral
nodes.statement: For the converse, assume \( \sigma = S^{\vee} \) for some finite \( S \subseteq M \). Then \( \Cone(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}.
nodes.statement_short: Conversely $\sigma=S^\vee$ and $\Cone(S)$ is polyhedral.

nodes.name: Find T
nodes.statement: Thus we find a finite \( T \subseteq N \) with \( \Cone(S) = T^\vee \).
nodes.statement_short: Choose finite $T$ with $\Cone(S)=T^\vee$.

nodes.name: Chain of equalities
nodes.statement: We obtain \[ \sigma = S^{\vee} = \Cone(S)^\vee = T^{\vee\vee} = \Cone(T), \] where the last equality is due to~\ref{double-dual-finite-set}.
nodes.statement_short: Chain $\sigma=T^{\vee\vee}=\Cone(T)$ via Proposition 9.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus \( \sigma \) is finitely generated.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $\sigma$ is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Easy inclusion and setup
nodes.statement: \( A^{\perp} \subseteq A^{\vee} \) is clear. Let \( x \in A^{\vee} \) and \( a \in A \). then \( \langle x, a \rangle \geq 0 \) and \( -\langle x, a \rangle = \langle x, -a \rangle \geq 0 \).
nodes.statement_short: Easy inclusion; for $x\in A^\vee$, pair with $a$ and $-a$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence \( \langle x, a \rangle = 0 \) and \( x \in A^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: Hence the pairing vanishes.

nodes.name: Write faces and claim
nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) and \( \tau' = \sigma \cap \tau'^{\perp} \) be faces. We claim that \( \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \cap u'^{\perp} = \sigma \cap (u + u')^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: Write the two faces and claim the intersection is cut out by $(u+u')^\perp$.

nodes.name: Converse setup
nodes.statement: The inclusion ``\( \subseteq \)'' is obvious. For the converse, suppose \( v \in \sigma \) with \( \langle v, u \rangle + \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \).
nodes.statement_short: Obvious inclusion; for the converse take $v$ with summed pairing zero.

nodes.name: Non-negativity
nodes.statement: Since \( u, u' \in \sigma^{\vee} \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle v, u \rangle = \langle v, u' \rangle = 0 \).
nodes.statement_short: Non-negative summands vanish.

nodes.name: Dualise span description
nodes.statement: It's easy to show that \( \tau = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau) \cap \sigma^{\vee} \). Dualising gives \( \tau^{\vee} = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} + \sigma^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Express $\tau$ via its span and dualise.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Apply~\ref{perp-closed-negation} to get \( \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\vee} = \Span_{\Bbbk}(\tau)^{\perp} = \tau^{\perp} \).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1 identifies the span's dual with $\tau^\perp$.

nodes.name: Decompose v
nodes.statement: Let \( \tau = \sigma \cap u^{\perp} \) with \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \) with \( v \in \tau^{\vee} \). By \ref{face-dual-eq-sum}, we can write \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) with \( v_1 \in \tau^{\perp} \) and \( v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \).
nodes.statement_short: Set up faces and decompose $v$ using Lemma 5.

nodes.name: Claim rho as face
nodes.statement: Then \( u + v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and we claim \( \rho = \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \). For ``\( \subseteq \)'', let \( x \in \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \). Since \( x \in \tau \), we get \( \langle x, u \rangle = 0 \) and \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). Since \( x \in v^{\perp} \), also \( \langle x, v \rangle = 0 \), which by \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) implies \( \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, u + v_2 \rangle = 0 \). For the converse, assume \( x \in \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \), i.e. \( \langle x, u \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). Since both \( u, v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( x \in \sigma \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle x, u \rangle = \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). This implies \( x \in \tau \), thus also \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, v \rangle = \langle x, v_1 \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \), thus \( x \in \rho \).
nodes.statement_short: Claim $\rho=\sigma\cap(u+v_2)^\perp$ and prove both inclusions.

nodes.name: Inclusion
nodes.statement: For ``\( \subseteq \)'', let \( x \in \rho = \tau \cap v^{\perp} \). Since \( x \in \tau \), we get \( \langle x, u \rangle = 0 \) and \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). Since \( x \in v^{\perp} \), also \( \langle x, v \rangle = 0 \), which by \( v = v_1 + v_2 \) implies \( \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, u + v_2 \rangle = 0 \).
nodes.statement_short: Forward inclusion by computing pairings.

nodes.name: Converse inclusion
nodes.statement: For the converse, assume \( x \in \sigma \cap (u + v_2)^{\perp} \), i.e. \( \langle x, u \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). Since both \( u, v_2 \in \sigma^{\vee} \) and \( x \in \sigma \), both summands are nonnegative, hence \( \langle x, u \rangle = \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \). This implies \( x \in \tau \), thus also \( \langle x, v_1 \rangle = 0 \). In total, \( \langle x, v \rangle = \langle x, v_1 \rangle + \langle x, v_2 \rangle = 0 \), thus \( x \in \rho \).
nodes.statement_short: Converse via non-negativity of summands.
